# Exploratory analysis

Goals - Identify the best threshold to remove noise; improve quantitative predictions from ML - plotting distributions

## Preliminary setup

```{r loadStuff}
library(tidyverse, quietly = TRUE)
library(magrittr) # for special Tee pipe operator %T>% (Error check, unique WT before calc)
library(patchwork) # for combining plots

# import functions
source("functions/0.data_processing.R")
source("functions/1.plotting.R")
source("functions/2.contribution_table.R")

# locate the data
base_path <- "enrichment_data/theoAptzepPCR_lokya/"
# file_path <- str_c(base_path, "subset.tsv") # for testing
file_path <- str_c(base_path, "DiMSum_Project_variant_data_merge.tsv") # for production

# global variables
expected_variants <- 135000 # (epPCR) from colony counts (source: Lokya)
count_tracker <- tibble(
  threshold = numeric(),
  variants = numeric(),
  input_reads = numeric(),
  filtered_columns = character()) # global variable to track counts at different thresholds
```

## Data cleanup

- Select relevant columns
- Clean up column names
- Calculate enrichment, leak metrics Ref: \_Borrowing some code from DiMSum/[split-multiinputs.R](https://github.com/ppreshant/DiMSum/blob/master/scripts/split_multiinputs.R)

```{r data-cleanup}
data <- read_and_cleanup_data(file_path)
cat("Column names: ", paste(colnames(data), collapse = ", "), "\n")

total_variants <- nrow(data)
total_reads <- sum(data$Input_count)

# count_tracker <- count_tracker |>

cat("Total variants: ", format(total_variants, big.mark = ","), "\n")
cat("Total reads: ", format(total_reads, big.mark = ","), "\n")
```

Plotting the distribution of reads in the raw data, selection counts, and leak counts. This will help us understand the distribution of reads across different categories.

```{r raw_read_distribution}
#| fig-width: 5
#| fig-height: 4

patch_read_dist_multi_columns(data) + 
  plot_annotation(title = "Distribution of reads in raw data",
                  subtitle = "Comparing input, selection and leak counts. Note log10 scale on y-axis")

```

Looking at the distribution of reads, we can see that there are a lot of variants with low counts. We want to filter out these low-count variants to reduce noise in our analysis.

# Filtering within Input, Selection, and Leak counts

Table of variant counts and input reads at different thresholds


```{r filter_set1_allthresholds}
thresholds <- c(0, 1, 2, 5, 10, 100)
filter_set_25 <- c("Input_count", "Selection_count", "Leak_count")

filter_list_25 <- 
  map(thresholds, 
    filter_data, df = data, filter_columns = filter_set_25)

count_log_25 <- bind_rows(count_tracker, 
  map(filter_list_25, \(x) x$count_tracker) |> 
  bind_rows())

```

## Distribution of reads at different thresholds

```{r read_distribution_25}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 7

read_distribution_25 <-
  map2(filter_list_25, thresholds, 
    \(x, t) patch_read_dist_multi_columns(x$filtered, title = str_c("count >= ", t))) |> 

    map(\(x) wrap_elements(full = x)) |> # freeze titles of each patch
    wrap_plots(ncol = 2, axes = "collect") |>
    plot_annotation(title = "Distribution of reads at different thresholds", subtitle = "Comparing input, selection and leak counts. Note log10 scale on y-axis")

read_distribution_25
  
```

# Indel analysis

## Read count distribution

```{r indel_read_distribution}
#| fig-width: 2
#| fig-height: 3
subset_data <- filter_list_25[[3]]$filtered # count >= 2

WT_len <- subset_data |>
  filter(Nham_nt == 0) |>
  pull(sequence_length) |>
  unique() # get WT length 

indels <- subset_data |>
  filter(is.na(Nham_nt)) |> # filter for indels
  mutate(indel_length = sequence_length - WT_len) # calculate indel length

read_distribution(indels)
```

## Variant distribution by sequence length

```{r indel_distribution_by_length}
#| fig-width: 4
#| fig-height: 5

# indel_variant_counts <- summarise(indels, count = n(), .by = indel_length) # summarize to get variant counts at each Nham_nt value

indel_variant_dist <- 
  ggplot(indels, aes(y = indel_length)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50, fill = "steelblue", colour = "black") + 
  # geom_hline(yintercept = 0) +
  # annotate("text", 
  #   x = 0.9 * max(indel_variant_counts$count),
  #   y = 0, 
  #   label = "WT length", 
  #   hjust = 1, vjust = -1) +
  labs(title = "Indel Variant Distribution by Sequence Length",
       x = "Number of Variants",
       y = "Indel Length (nt)") +
  theme_minimal()

# indel read distr
indel_read_counts <- summarise(indels, count = sum(Input_count), .by = indel_length) # summarize to get variant counts at each Nham_nt value

indel_read_dist <- 
  ggplot(indel_read_counts, aes(x = count, y = indel_length)) +
  geom_point(size = 2, color = "steelblue") +
  # xlim(0, 5000)
  scale_x_log10() +
  # geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "steelblue") + 
  labs(title = "Indel Read Distribution by Sequence Length",
       x = "Number of Reads",
       y = "Indel Length (nt)") +
  theme_minimal()

# combine the two plots
indel_variant_dist + indel_read_dist + plot_layout(axes = "collect") + 
  plot_annotation(title = "Indel Variant and Read Distribution by Sequence Length",
                  subtitle = "Comparing number of variants and number of reads for each indel length. Note log10 scale on x-axis for read distribution")
```

# Selecting variants of interest 

Selecting variants that span the distribution of net_catalysis scores for individual testing (with fluorescence, flow cytometry)
1. Order the data by net_catalysis score
2. Select score-quantile bin boundaries separately above and below WT
3. Select the variants with max selection_freq within each bin (to ensure good coverage/representation within the library for individual testing)


```{r select_variants_of_interest}
subset_data <- filter_data(data, 2)$filtered # count >= 2

ranked_catalysis <- subset_data |>
  arrange(desc(net_catalysis)) |>
  mutate(rank = row_number())

nrow(ranked_catalysis)

# WT rank
wt_rank <- filter(ranked_catalysis, Nham_nt == 0) |> pull(rank) |> print()
```

Rank of the WT variant is `{r} wt_rank`. Check the distribution of net_catalysis scores for the selection set and the total set.

```{r}
dcomb <- bind_rows(
  ranked_catalysis |> select(net_catalysis) |> mutate(set = "b. selection"),
  subset_data |> select(net_catalysis) |> mutate(set = "a. total d2")
)

ggplot(dcomb, aes(x = net_catalysis, fill = set)) +
  geom_histogram(position = "identity", alpha = 0.5, bins = 50) +
  scale_x_log10() +

  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.5) +
  annotate(geom = "text", x = 0.5, y = 0, label = "WT", vjust = -1) +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Net Catalysis Scores",
       x = "Net Catalysis (WT normalized)",
       y = "Frequency") +
  theme_minimal()
```

The distribution does look distorted but we don't need it to be representative; as much as pick variants with high coverage.

The table below shows the selected variants of interest for individual testing.


```{r}
# Create score-quantile bins separately above and below WT. Define WT itself
# independently so it is not counted in or duplicated by an adjacent bin.
make_score_quantile_bins <- function(x, n_bins) {
  breaks <- quantile(
    x,
    probs = seq(0, 1, length.out = n_bins + 1),
    na.rm = TRUE,
    names = FALSE,
    type = 8
  ) |> unique()

  if (length(breaks) < 2L) {
    return(rep(1L, length(x)))
  }

  cut(x, breaks = breaks, include.lowest = TRUE, labels = FALSE)
}

wt_row <- ranked_catalysis |>
  filter(rank == wt_rank)

non_wt_variants <- ranked_catalysis |>
  filter(rank != wt_rank) |>
  mutate(
    region = if_else(rank < wt_rank, "above WT", "below WT"),
    bin = NA_integer_
  )

non_wt_variants <- non_wt_variants |>
  group_by(region) |>
  group_modify(
    ~ .x |> mutate(
      bin = make_score_quantile_bins(
        net_catalysis,
        n_bins = if (.y$region == "above WT") 7L else 3L
      )
    )
  ) |>
  ungroup()

selected_from_bins <- non_wt_variants |>
  group_by(region, bin) |>
  slice_max(
    order_by = Selection_count,
    n = 1,
    with_ties = FALSE,
    na_rm = TRUE
  ) |>
  ungroup()

selected <- bind_rows(wt_row, selected_from_bins) |>
  arrange(rank) |>
  distinct(nt_seq, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  select(nt_seq, rank, net_catalysis, relative_catalysis, relative_leak,
         Nham_nt, region, bin, Selection_count, everything())

# save to csv
write_csv(selected, str_c(base_path, "selected_variants_of_interest.csv"))

# Show formatted data
mutate(selected, 
  across(where(is.numeric),
    \(x) signif(x, 2) |> 
          format(big.mark = ",") )) |>

knitr::kable(caption = "Selected variants of interest for individual testing")

```

Visualize the selected data on the catalysis vs leak plot to see where they fall in the distribution.

```{r}

cat_leak_plot <-
  ggplot(subset_data,
    aes(y = relative_catalysis, x = relative_leak,
    size = log10(Selection_count), colour = ntile(desc(net_catalysis), 4))) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2) +
  # scale_alpha_manual(values = c(10.1, 0.2, 0.25, 0.3)) +
  scale_x_log10() + scale_y_log10() +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, color = "red") +
  labs(title = "Comparison of Catalysis and Leak Scores",
        y = "Catalysis, WT normalized",
        x = "Leak, WT normalized") +
  theme_minimal()

cat_leak_plot

cat_leak_plot +
  geom_point(data = selected, color = "red", size = 2) +
  geom_text(data = selected, aes(y = relative_catalysis, x = relative_leak, label = rank), color = "red", vjust = -1, size = 3) +
  labs(title = "Selected Variants of Interest on Catalysis vs Leak Plot",
       subtitle = "Red points indicate selected variants for individual testing")

```


## Send thresholded data to Dylan
Remove insertions and deletions, and save separate files for each threshold. This will be used for individual testing of variants.


```{r}
# create path if it doesn't exist
dylan_files <- str_c(base_path, "dylan_files/")
if (!dir.exists(dylan_files)) {
  dir.create(dylan_files, recursive = TRUE)
}

total_variants <- nrow(data)

map2(filter_list_25, thresholds, 
  \(x, t) {
    filtered_data <- x$filtered |>
      filter(!is.na(Nham_nt)) # remove indels
  
  # report the percentage of total variants that pass the threshold    
  cat("threshold >= ", t, ": ", format(nrow(filtered_data)/total_variants * 100, digits = 2), " % of total variants\n")
  cat("\t Retains: ", format(nrow(filtered_data), big.mark = ","), " variants\n\n")

    write_csv(filtered_data, str_c(dylan_files, "filtered_threshold_", t, ".csv"))
  })
```
